description:
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): the extras-preservation policy section in workspace AGENTS.md must be narrowed to exclude classifier-attribute strings on data-object sub-types in type crates that mirror an externally-owned schema (JSContact via RFC 9553; JSCalendar via RFC 8984).

## Rationale

RFC 9553 and RFC 8984 enumerate classifier strings (e.g. `Title.kind`, `NameComponent.kind`, `Anniversary.kind`, `Participant.kind`, `RecurrenceRule.frequency`) as if those enumerations were authoritative. Operational reality in the contacts and calendars ecosystems is that real implementers (Outlook, Google, Apple, vCard exporters, localized clients, third-party CalDAV servers, etc.) routinely send strings outside the spec enumeration. Typing these into `enum { Variant1, Variant2, ..., Other(String) }` creates a fiction where the catch-all does most of the real work and the named variants do ~no programmatic dispatch. The maintenance cost (variant additions on every spec revision, `#[non_exhaustive]` surface, propagation through consumers) is paid for no programmatic benefit.

## In-scope policy stays the same for JMAP-native enums

`MailboxRole`, `DeliveryState`, `NodeType`, `EmojiKind`, `ChatKind`, `ParticipantRole` etc. remain in scope for the typed-enum-with-`Unknown(String)` mechanism. These are JMAP-defined wire-format result enums on JMAP-native types; consumers DO dispatch reliably on them; the wild-vendor-extensions pattern does not apply.

## Site

`/home/mark/PROJECT/JMAP/AGENTS.md`, the section titled 'Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields', sub-list 'In scope (apply both mechanisms)'.

## Proposed wording (illustrative; bead claimant may refine)

Add an explicit excluded-from-scope bullet under the existing 'Out of scope' list, OR add a new sub-section after the 'In scope' list. Suggested text:

> **Excluded: classifier-attribute strings on data-object sub-types in type crates that mirror an externally-owned schema.**
>
> Examples: `NameComponent.kind`, `Title.kind`, `Calendar.kind`, `Anniversary.kind`, `PersonalInfo.kind` in `jmap-jscontact-types`; `Participant.kind`, `RecurrenceRule.frequency`, `Alert.action` in `jmap-jscalendar-types`.
>
> Rationale: the RFCs that define these schemas (RFC 9553 JSContact, RFC 8984 JSCalendar) enumerate classifier values as if authoritative. Operational reality is that real-world implementers routinely send values outside the spec enumeration. Typed enums with `Other(String)` catch-all create a fiction where the catch-all does most of the work and named variants do no programmatic dispatch. Leave these fields as `Option<String>` or `String`; consumers that care about specific values match string literals.
>
> This exclusion is narrow. It does NOT apply to:
> - JMAP-native result enums (`MailboxRole`, `ChatKind`, etc.) — those stay in scope.
> - Field shapes that are whole nested objects — those follow the Sloppy-Value pattern.
> - Wire-protocol control values defined by RFC 8620 itself — those stay in scope.

## Acceptance

  - Workspace AGENTS.md edit lands with the exclusion text (final wording at claimant's discretion as long as it matches the rationale above).
  - JMAP-sc1b.110 (jscalendar-types revert) cross-links to this bead as the policy basis.
  - JMAP-sc1b.108 (jscontact-types propagation) cross-links to this bead as the policy basis for closing wontfix.
  - No code changes — workspace AGENTS.md only.

## Cross-references

  - JMAP-sc1b.77 — the original jscalendar-types conversion that this exclusion makes wrong in retrospect
  - JMAP-sc1b.108 — the parallel jscontact-types propagation that triggered the policy discussion
title: Workspace AGENTS.md: narrow extras-section scope to exclude externally-owned-schema classifier strings
